newsitem.title: USA: Minn. Governor sets session for education funding.
newsitem.headline: Minn. Governor sets session for education funding.

text.p: Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson announced Wednesday he will call lawmakers back for a special session on June 26 to reach an accord on education funding issues.
Carlson vetoed the two-year $6.7 billion elementary and secondary education spending package earlier this month because it lacked tuition tax credits he has proposed.
"We need fundamental reforms to reverse the alarming test score and drop out trends we are seeing in Minnesota," Carlson said in a statement.

Carlson has called for $150 million in tax credits for education that would triple current deductions. The credits could be used for hiring a tutor, summer school programs or purchase of a home computer as well as tuition to private schools.
